key_insight: The paper argues that AI, especially LLMs, could help citizens’ assemblies and other deliberative democratic processes, but only if used under explicit philosophical and democratic constraints.
engineering_relevance: For AI system designers, the main challenge is building LLM tools for moderation, translation, summarization, and facilitation that can be audited for political bias and aligned with democratic norms.
method: Interdisciplinary framework combining philosophy and computer science
Evaluates LLMs against five proposed democratic principles
Focuses on the question of political bias in citizen-participation settings
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a normative, evaluative project rather than reporting a dataset or experiment, using democratic principles to assess when LLMs can be used legitimately in citizen deliberation.
watch_item: The main implementation concern is that LLM outputs may embed political bias or undermine legitimacy if democratic safeguards and epistemic caution are not built in.
paper_title: New Conditions for Philosophers to Catch the Wave of Citizen Deliberation in the Age of Artificial Intelligence in advance
